books.title: Amp It Up
books.author: Frank Slootman
takeaways: Amp it Up means raise standards and expectations - never half-ass anything, always overdeliver
Hire for grit, drive, and learning speed - these matter more than credentials
Focus on the SINGLE most important thing and eliminate noise - clarity over consensus
Execution >>>>> Strategy - be a driver with personal ownership, not a passive passenger
Be quick to fire and weed out - culture is made by what and who you tolerate

books.title: How to Win Friends and Influence People
books.author: Dale Carnegie
takeaways: Don't criticize, condemn, or complain - change people's attitudes by changing yours first
Give honest and sincere appreciation - look for the good in people and tell them
Remember and use people's names - it's fundamental to building relationships
Be a great listener and show genuine interest - listening is as important as speaking
Smile and bring energy to every interaction - happiness depends on mental attitude, not circumstances
Be patient and make people feel valued - every person is superior to you in some way

books.title: Wooden on Leadership
books.author: John Wooden
takeaways: Failing to prepare is preparing to fail - make every day your masterpiece
Care about your character (who you are), not your reputation (what others think)
Keep peaks and valleys balanced - things don't get easier, you get tougher
Don't let what you cannot do interfere with what you can do
Discipline yourself so others won't need to - family comes first

books.title: High Performance Habits
books.author: Brendon Burchard
takeaways: Seek clarity on who you are, what you want, and practice being your future self now
Manage energy like an athlete - sleep, movement, and mental clarity are non-negotiable
Build necessity through environment - you fall to the level of your surroundings
Focus on five needle-moving actions and optimize them relentlessly
Demonstrate courage through action - movement dissolves fear and adversity builds strength

books.title: The Millionaire Fastlane
books.author: M.J DeMarco
takeaways: Three paths to wealth: Sidewalk (spend>earn), Slow lane (trade time for wealth), Fastlane (entrepreneurship for freedom and wealth while young)
The process makes the money, not the event - you can't outsource the struggle, earn your stripes
Build money trees for passive income: Rental systems (A+), Software (A), Content (B+), Distribution (B), Human systems (C+)
Solve problems the market will pay for - don't build what you love, build what people need
Live below your means while expanding your means - maximize income, not minimize expenses
Execution is king - embrace failure, master financial literacy, and take massive action

books.title: Meditations
books.author: Marcus Aurelius
takeaways: We filter our thoughts based on others' opinions constantly, even unconsciously - ask whether you're doing something because you want to or because it feels safe
Death is as natural as birth and aging - life is a rent borrowed from nature that must eventually be returned, nothing more to dwell on
Stoicism's core flaw: it teaches safety and enduring pain, not how to enjoy life - humans need humans, not just protection and provision
Don't be angered by people's flaws - a bad person being bad is expected; correct others out of humility to help them, not to boast
The shortness of life is a fact and everything happens for a reason - accept nature's course and you won't waste time in angst
Another flaw in stoicism: it overestimates the power of logic alone - some of history's most logical people have also been its cruelest
The only thing standing between you and what you want to achieve is you yourself
Meditations was never intended for publication, it was Marcus's private journal - its values serve an individual well but can't be anyone's sole compass
